facts.Foundshore Verdict: Strong fit for undergraduate frontier-technology builders.
facts.Focus: Computational biology, AI infrastructure, advanced materials, aerospace, defense, frontier technology
facts.Funding / Support: US$15K non-dilutive grant + Lux mentorship + fully covered retreats
facts.Geography / Affiliation Restriction: Undergraduate student; nationality not restricted on 2026 page
facts.Official / Must-Have Requirements: Undergraduate builders independently experimenting with frontier technology; incorporation is not required.
facts.Strong-to-Have: Existing research, prototypes, experiments, open-source contributions or laboratory work demonstrating technical commitment.
facts.On-site / Attendance: Two fully covered retreats: a New York kickoff and September Fellows Summit. Other mentorship arrangements are flexible.
facts.International Founder: Yes — 2025 fellows nearly half international; 2026 page does not restrict nationality
facts.Visa / Relocation: No long-term relocation required; lawful US entry is needed for retreats.
facts.Public Contact Route: Official fellowship application; general public email available.
facts.Foundshore Best Fit: Undergraduates independently building frontier-technology experiments, tools or research, including those without a company, seeking non-dilutive funding and Lux mentorship.
facts.Foundshore Not Fit: Non-undergraduates, mature startups, lightweight consumer apps or applicants seeking credentials without independent building or research.
facts.Notes: A pre-founder fellowship rather than a startup accelerator, especially relevant to students turning frontier research into companies.
